metaDescription: Arrowhead Springs sits on Union Pacific checkerboard ground in Sweetwater County. Learn how odd/even section ownership affects your mineral rights before you sell.
heroLead: Arrowhead Springs sits on the checkerboard, the odd-numbered sections railroad land grant that runs the length of Sweetwater County, and figuring out which color square your tract falls in is the first thing I check.
intro: Congress granted the Union Pacific alternating sections along its right-of-way back in the 1860s to help finance the railroad, and those grants became private land, private minerals in many cases, while the sections in between stayed federal. That pattern still governs ownership across this whole corridor, and Sweetwater County land near Rock Springs and Green River is some of the most checkerboarded ground in the state.

If your family's interest traces to a UP land grant, you own private minerals outright, no BLM lease process, no federal royalty schedule. If it's on an even section, the story is different, and I'll tell you which one applies to you.

sections.heading: Reading the checkerboard
paragraphs: Odd sections in this railroad grant corridor were typically patented to the Union Pacific and later sold off, often with both surface and minerals conveyed together or split by later deed. Even sections stayed under federal ownership, meaning any oil and gas there is BLM-administered minerals, developed through a federal lease process with a fixed statutory royalty, separate from private mineral deals entirely.
I've seen family ownership span both kinds within a single section line, which is why I always confirm the specific quarter section before saying anything about value.

sections.heading: What this area has seen
paragraphs: Sweetwater County's Green River Basin activity runs from the Jonah and Pinedale trend to the north down through Continental Divide-Creston gas development closer to Arrowhead Springs. Much of the natural gas production near here has come from tight sands developed with denser well spacing than older Wyoming fields, run mostly by mid-size independent operators over the past two decades.

sections.heading: Confirming private mineral ownership
paragraphs: For a private (odd-section) tract, I check the Sweetwater County recorder for your chain of title back to the original UP patent or land grant sale, then confirm any current lease status. That establishes clean title before we ever discuss a number.

faqs.question: How do I know if my section is odd or even?
faqs.answer: Send me your legal description or deed and I'll check it against the county plat myself.

faqs.question: Can I sell minerals under a federal (even) section?
faqs.answer: If your minerals are federally owned, there's nothing private to sell there. If you hold a private interest adjacent to or checkerboarded with federal land, that private piece is what we'd discuss.

faqs.question: Is there active gas production near Arrowhead Springs?
faqs.answer: Sweetwater County has ongoing tight-gas development in several trends. I'll check whether your specific section has lease or production history.
